To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the QLL framework provides a classification of customer integration tools that allows companies to select the most appropriate tools for their NPD purposes; (ii) the QLL classification is receptive to the knowledge requirements of NPD projects, and (iii) the framework allows the selection of the most appropriate methods to be made on the basis of the explicitness and complexity of the knowledge exchanged throughout the project.
the selection of methods for virtual customer integration should take into account the type of knowledge that needs to be transferred, and the stage of the NPD process where the transfer takes place.
the most important criteria in the choice of a customer integration method are the type of knowledge required and the degree of explicitness and tacitness of the knowledge.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a practical problem that is of high importance to many firms, namely, how to select the most appropriate customer integration methods and to which extent they should be applied.
how and when to use conventional and virtual methods in the NPD process and on what grounds.
the question of how and when companies should make use of virtual and conventional customer integration methods in their NPD projects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
virtual customer integration tools have their place, but that they cannot replace face to face customer interaction.
virtual customer integration is not a panacea for all customer integration problems, but that it can offer a promising new tool for industrial companies in certain circumstances.

the use of conventional and/or virtual customer integration tools is dependent on the knowledge transfer requirements in each stage of the NPD process, the explicitness and the tacitness of the knowledge to be transferred, and the specific characteristics of each NPD project.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

virtual methods for customer collaboration are not an alternative to conventional methods, but a complement that can be used in the right circumstances to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of the new product development process.
virtual customer integration is not a panacea.
the classification of customer integration is not only a question of the type of information that needs to be shared, but also a question of how this knowledge is best shared, and when.
The main takeaway from our work is that
companies need to be aware that different customer integration methods are more appropriate for different stages in the NPD process and for different kinds of knowledge.
the choice of a customer integration method should not be taken in isolation.
virtual methods can be a powerful tool for customer integration, but only if the knowledge exchange requirements of the particular NPD project are taken into account.
